goal: Replace Boost.Test with an in-house header-only unit test runner to improve test diagnostics and eliminate a Boost dependency.
Unify inconsistent test assertion macros and enable future test framework features like parallel test execution.

result.summary: Replaces Boost.Test with a custom, in-house header-only testing framework in src/test/util/framework.h. Migrates all unit test suites across the repository to the new framework via scripted diff while retaining macro compatibility shims. Removes Boost.Test configuration from depends, CMake, vcpkg, and Guix scripts.
result.problem: Boost.Test suffers from inconsistent assertion macros, poor diagnostic messages when expressions fail without custom stream operators, and lack of integration with Bitcoin Core types and execution needs. Developers also carry recurring maintenance overhead in build scripts and Guix workarounds for Boost.Test quirks.

resolved_concerns: Compile-time static assertions when string representations are missing for compared types (maflcko).
Undefined behavior or segfaults on null C-string comparisons (jeanpablojp).
Buffering issues losing crash diagnostic output and seed reproducibility under randomized test runs (jeanpablojp).
Retention of fatal linker warning flags in Guix build scripts after removing Boost workarounds (jeanpablojp, fanquake).

result.card: This pull request replaces the Boost.Test unit test framework with a tailored, header-only test runner located in src/test/util/framework.h and updates all unit test files via scripted diff. It addresses longstanding limitations of Boost.Test including unintuitive assertion macros, uninformative failure messages, and awkward external integration, while eliminating Boost.Test from depends and CI builds. Strong support has been voiced by reviewers who note that an in-house framework will improve test diagnostics and enable future architectural enhancements such as test concurrency. The PR is clean, well-tested, and actively maintained with no blocking objections.
